newsitem.title: UK: Bangladeshi butter output best guide to S&P 500.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshi butter output best guide to S&P 500.

text.p: Investors searching for an alternative, if unusual, guide to trends in U.S. equities may have found a new source -- Bangladeshi butter.
When butter production goes up, so does the Standard & Poor's 500 index.

Butter production in Bangladesh turned out to be the single best predictor of the performance of the S&P 500 index in a recent 10 year period, according to Robert Brown, a director at UK-based investment adviser First Quadrant.
First Quadrant examined United Nations statistics on "thousands of sets of economic data and indicators", Brown said.

Using "massively parallel computing", a technique employed by IBM Deep Blue in its recent defeat of chess champion Garry Kasparov, the study made billions of separate operations to reach the comparison, he said.
"You have a fantastic fit," Brown said.
But he cautioned against using Bangladesh butter production to predict the S&P 500 going forward, saying there was absolutely no fundamental relationship between the two.
